The Commercial Vehicle Model (CVM) generates daily Light (LT), Medium (MD), and Heavy
(HV) commercial-vehicle trips for six vocations -- Door-to-Door (D2D), Hub-and-Spoke
(HnS), Local (Lcl), Regional (Reg), Long-Haul (LHl), and Unknown (Unk) -- from trip-rate
models built on LOCUS commercial-vehicle data. Those raw rates rarely match observed
commercial-vehicle activity exactly, so a set of calibration factors are layered on
top, by county and (for MD/HV) by vocation. This page breaks down, for the selected
calibration run, how
much of the region's final commercial-vehicle trips and VMT trace back to the raw
LOCUS-based rates ("base model") versus how much comes from that calibration
adjustment -- and separately explains what falls **outside** the CVM entirely: the
external (X) end of any trip that crosses the region boundary.

## About the LOCUS Data

UDOT has licensed commercial-vehicle origin-destination (OD) data from LOCUS that was
geo-referenced to the region's TAZs and external stations, made available to WFRC as
part of a 2025 Wasatch Front TDM Truck Model Update effort. That project used the
licensed LOCUS OD data, alongside segment-level roadway volumes with medium- and
heavy-duty commercial-vehicle percentages and a base- and horizon-year commercial-vehicle
trip table extracted from the Utah Statewide Travel Demand Model (USTM), to re-estimate
and calibrate the CVM's internal (II) trip generation and distribution parameters
against 2023 base-year observed commercial-vehicle activity. Per the
LOCUS-derived `CV TG Rates.csv` rate table, that re-estimation also reaches the
internal-zone side of IX/XI trip generation (see "Within-region distribution" further
down this page). Consistent with the project's scope, though, USTM continues to supply
XX trip tables and the external end zones for IX/XI trips; LOCUS data doesn't reach
those.

**A note on vehicle-class definitions.** LOCUS classifies commercial vehicles by gross
vehicle weight, while UDOT's roadway count data -- including the Continuous Count
Station (CCS) adjustments described below -- classifies by vehicle configuration:
single-unit (SU) vs. multi-unit (MU). The two schemes don't always agree. A short,
rigid single-unit vehicle like a dump truck or concrete mixer can carry a gross vehicle
weight well into LOCUS's "Heavy" bucket while still counting as UDOT's shorter
single-unit ("Medium") category at a count station. Vehicles like these are a possible
source of any mismatch between the CVM's LOCUS-derived Medium/Heavy split and UDOT's
own Medium/Heavy percentages.

```{python}
# ==============================================================================
# LOAD PER-RUN CVM FACTORING DATA
# ==============================================================================
# Unlike the other report pages, this data isn't part of the normal curated
# runs/ output or report/preprocess/ cache -- computing it requires converting
# raw Cube .mtx matrices via Voyager (see scripts/cv_purpose_factoring.py's
# module docstring), which is too slow to do on every `quarto render`. Instead
# that script is run manually per calibration run and its output committed
# here as a small static CSV, same as any other report/data/ input. Not every
# run in runs/ has had the script run against it yet, so `calib_runs` (below)
# stays the same full site-wide list every other report page offers -- the
# shared calibration-run selector (_calib_run_selector.qmd) always shows every
# available run, greying out this page's own sidebar entry when the selected
# run has no CVM data rather than shrinking the dropdown itself. The
# CVM-specific subset lives in `cvm_available_runs` instead, used only to
# decide what this page itself can render.
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import _validation_scripts as vs

repo_root = Path("..")
calib_runs = vs.list_available_runs(repo_root)

data_dir = Path("data/cvm-update")
files = sorted(data_dir.glob("purpose_factoring_*.csv"))
cvm_df = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f) for f in files], ignore_index=True) if files else pd.DataFrame()
cvm_available_runs = sorted(cvm_df["calib_run"].unique().tolist(), key=lambda s: int("".join(c for c in s if c.isdigit()) or 0)) if not cvm_df.empty else []

ojs_define(cvm_data=cvm_df, cvm_available_runs=cvm_available_runs)
```

```{ojs}
allRows = transpose(cvm_data)
vocOrder = ["D2D", "HnS", "Lcl", "Reg", "LHl", "Unk"]
```

## Total Commercial Vehicle Activity

Trips and VMT below cover **all** commercial-vehicle movement -- internal (II),
plus any trip with one or both ends outside the region (IX/XI/XX). Each card
splits that total into what the raw model would have produced on its own
("base model") versus the net effect of every calibration factor applied on
top ("adjustment") -- a negative adjustment means calibration is scaling the
raw estimate *down*, not up.

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-cvm-headline
//| fig-cap: "Total Commercial Vehicle Trips and VMT by Vehicle Type"

function headlineCard(veh) {
  const vehRows = rows.filter(d => d.vehicle_type === veh);
  function totals(metric) {
    const m = vehRows.filter(d => d.metric === metric);
    const factored = d3.sum(m, d => d.factored);
    const unfactored = d3.sum(m, d => d.unfactored);
    return { factored, unfactored, modelPct: factored ? unfactored / factored * 100 : 0, adjPct: factored ? (factored - unfactored) / factored * 100 : 0 };
  }
  const trips = totals("trips");
  const vmt = totals("vmt");

  const row = (label, t) => html`<div style="display:flex; justify-content:space-between; padding:3px 0;">
    <span style="color:${themeNeutral};">${label}</span>
    <span><strong>${fmtInt(t.factored)}</strong> &nbsp;<span style="color:${themeNeutral}; font-size:0.9em;">(${fmtPct(t.modelPct)}% model / ${t.adjPct >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${fmtPct(t.adjPct)}% adj)</span></span>
  </div>`;

  return html`<div style="border:1px solid #e0dfdd; border-radius:8px; padding:14px 18px; flex:1; min-width:240px;">
    <div style="font-weight:600; font-size:1.05em; margin-bottom:6px;">${vehicleLabel.get(veh)}</div>
    ${row("Daily Trips", trips)}
    ${row("Daily VMT", vmt)}
  </div>`;
}

html`<div style="display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:12px;">
  ${vehicleOrder.map(headlineCard)}
</div>`
```

The table below splits that same total into its two sources -- internal
(II) trips from the CVM rate model versus external (IX/XI/XX) trips from
the gateway-station process described further down this page -- using each
run's final, fully-calibrated values.

```{ojs}
//| label: tbl-cvm-total-summary

function iiExtTotal(veh, metric) {
  const m = rows.filter(d => d.vehicle_type === veh && d.metric === metric);
  const ii = d3.sum(m.filter(d => vocOrder.includes(d.component)), d => d.factored);
  const ext = d3.sum(m.filter(d => extOrder.includes(d.component)), d => d.factored);
  return { ii, ext, total: ii + ext };
}

html`
<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      ${["Vehicle Type", "Metric", "Internal (II)", "External (IX/XI/XX)", "Total Commercial Vehicle Activity"].map(d =>
        html`<th style='text-align:left; padding:5px;'>${d}</th>`)}
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    ${vehicleOrder.flatMap(veh => ["trips", "vmt"].map(metric => {
      const t = iiExtTotal(veh, metric);
      return html`<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid lightgrey;'>
        <td style='padding:5px;'>${vehicleLabel.get(veh)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px;'>${metric === "trips" ? "Daily Trips" : "Daily VMT"}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(t.ii)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(t.ext)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'><strong>${fmtInt(t.total)}</strong></td>
      </tr>`;
    }))}
    ${["trips", "vmt"].map(metric => {
      const totals = vehicleOrder.map(veh => iiExtTotal(veh, metric));
      const ii = d3.sum(totals, d => d.ii);
      const ext = d3.sum(totals, d => d.ext);
      return html`<tr style='border-top: 2px solid #999; font-weight:600;'>
        <td style='padding:5px;'>All Vehicle Types</td>
        <td style='padding:5px;'>${metric === "trips" ? "Daily Trips" : "Daily VMT"}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(ii)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(ext)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(ii + ext)}</td>
      </tr>`;
    })}
  </tbody>
</table>`
```

## Base Model vs. Calibration Adjustment, by Purpose

Each purpose below is one of the six LOCUS-derived vocations, **internal
(II) trips only** -- the only place a purpose-specific calibration factor
applies (see the section below for IX/XI/XX, which are calibrated by a
different, vocation-blind mechanism entirely). The dot marked "Base Model"
is what the raw LOCUS trip-rate model alone would produce; "Final
(Calibrated)" is this run's actual output after every calibration factor is
applied. The percent label is the calibration factor's net effect.

```{ojs}
//| panel: input
viewof cvmMetric = Inputs.radio(["trips", "vmt"], {value: "trips", label: "Metric:", format: d => d === "trips" ? "Trip Generation" : "VMT"})
```

```{ojs}
// Legend is its own independent cell (not referenced from inside the chart
// cell below) so that if it fails to evaluate -- e.g. Observable's CDN
// (@d3/color-legend) being unreachable -- only this swatch is affected, not
// the charts themselves. Same decoupling 3-modechoice.qmd's transit
// dumbbell legend uses.
import {Legend} from "@d3/color-legend"

cvmColorScale = d3.scaleOrdinal(["Base Model", "Final (Calibrated)"], [themeNeutral, themeModel])
keyCvmPurpose = Legend(cvmColorScale, {title: ""})
```

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-cvm-purpose-dumbbell
//| fig-cap: "Base Model vs. Final Calibrated -- Internal (II) Trips/VMT by Vocation"

function purposeDumbbell(veh) {
  const data = vocOrder.map(voc => {
    const r = rows.find(d => d.vehicle_type === veh && d.component === voc && d.metric === cvmMetric);
    return r ? { Purpose: voc, Model: r.unfactored, Final: r.factored, pctAdj: (r.factored - r.unfactored) / r.factored * 100 } : { Purpose: voc, Model: 0, Final: 0, pctAdj: 0 };
  });
  const xMax = d3.max(data, d => Math.max(d.Model, d.Final)) || 1;
  const xLabel = cvmMetric === "trips" ? "Daily Trips" : "Daily VMT";

  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: 340,
    height: 220,
    marginLeft: 55,
    marginRight: 55,
    marginTop: 8,
    y: {domain: vocOrder, label: null},
    x: {label: xLabel, domain: [0, xMax], grid: true, nice: true, tickFormat: "~s"},
    marks: [
      Plot.link(data, {x1: "Model", x2: "Final", y: "Purpose", stroke: themeLinkGrey, strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "Model", y: "Purpose", fill: themeNeutral, r: 7, title: d => `${d.Purpose}\nBase Model: ${fmtInt(d.Model)}`}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "Final", y: "Purpose", fill: themeModel, r: 7, title: d => `${d.Purpose}\nFinal: ${fmtInt(d.Final)}`}),
      Plot.text(data.filter(d => d.Final >= d.Model), {x: "Final", y: "Purpose", text: d => d3.format("+.0f")(d.pctAdj) + "%", dx: 10, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 600, fill: themeNeutral}),
      Plot.text(data.filter(d => d.Final < d.Model), {x: "Final", y: "Purpose", text: d => d3.format("+.0f")(d.pctAdj) + "%", dx: -10, textAnchor: "end", fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 600, fill: themeNeutral}),
    ],
  });
  return html`<div>
    <div style="font-weight:600; text-align:center; margin-bottom:2px;">${vehicleLabel.get(veh)}</div>
    ${chart}
  </div>`;
}

html`<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap; justify-content:center;">${vehicleOrder.map(purposeDumbbell)}</div>`
```

```{ojs}
html`
<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      ${["Vehicle Type", "Purpose", "Base Model", "Final (Calibrated)", "Adjustment Factor", "% Model / % Adjustment"].map(d =>
        html`<th style='text-align:left; padding:5px;'>${d}</th>`)}
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    ${vehicleOrder.flatMap(veh => vocOrder.map(voc => {
      const r = rows.find(d => d.vehicle_type === veh && d.component === voc && d.metric === cvmMetric);
      if (!r) return html``;
      return html`<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid lightgrey;'>
        <td style='padding:5px;'>${vehicleLabel.get(veh)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px;'>${voc}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(r.unfactored)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(r.factored)}</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtFactor(r.effective_factor)}x</td>
        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtPct(r.unfactored / r.factored * 100)}% / ${(r.factored - r.unfactored) / r.factored >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${fmtPct((r.factored - r.unfactored) / r.factored * 100)}%</td>
      </tr>`;
    }))}
  </tbody>
</table>`
```

## What's Not Part of the CVM: External (X-End) Trips

Not every commercial-vehicle trip touching our region comes from the CVM
rate model above. Any trip with an external end -- **IX** (internal
origin, external destination), **XI** (external origin, internal
destination), or **XX** (passing through, both ends external) -- has its
*volume* set independently of that rate model, though the CVM's own data
still shapes part of where those trips land:

- **Trip generation**: overall AADT at each external gateway station is
  forecast from HPMS segment AADT volumes, then split into medium- and
  heavy-duty commercial-vehicle volumes using base-year UDOT medium-/heavy-duty
  commercial-vehicle percentages -- themselves adjusted using revised
  vehicle-length classifications at nearby Continuous Count Stations (CCS).
  Not a LOCUS-derived rate model.
- **Within-region distribution** (which internal zone originates an IX
  trip, or receives an XI trip): shaped by the same land-use-based rate
  table (`CV TG Rates.csv`, LOCUS-derived) used for internal CVM trips --
  but for *shape only*. Those zone-level values are immediately rescaled so
  the region-wide IX/XI total matches the AADT-derived external total from
  above, so LOCUS data has no influence on *how much* IX/XI volume exists,
  only *where within the region* it starts or ends.
- **Gateway/route pattern** (which external station an IX/XI trip uses, and
  for XX, which entry-and-exit gateway pair): a separate historical
  subarea-extraction pattern, not LOCUS/CVM data and not a live run of the
  Utah Statewide model.

The only calibration applied to these trips is a per-station, per-vehicle-type
multiplier (`calibFac_Ext_MD_<station>` / `calibFac_Ext_HV_<station>`) that
scales a station's whole commercial-vehicle volume before splitting it into
IX/XI/XX shares -- there's no vocation dimension here (LOCUS's
D2D/HnS/Lcl/Reg/LHl/Unk split doesn't apply), and no LT component at all
(Light commercial vehicles are folded
into the passenger-vehicle volume at external stations, which get their own
separate `calibFac_Ext_PL_<station>` multiplier). These factors are
derived by comparing the resulting link volumes, once forecast, against each
station's CCS Fall 2023 weekday average volume -- the difference becomes the
adjustment factor, so like the rest of the CVM's calibration they're anchored
to actual observed station counts rather than a demand-rate model.

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-cvm-external
//| fig-cap: "External (IX/XI/XX) Trips/VMT by Vehicle Type -- Not CVM/LOCUS-Derived"

function externalDumbbell(veh) {
  const data = extOrder.map(comp => {
    const r = rows.find(d => d.vehicle_type === veh && d.component === comp && d.metric === cvmMetric);
    return r ? { Purpose: comp, Model: r.unfactored, Final: r.factored, pctAdj: (r.factored - r.unfactored) / r.factored * 100 } : { Purpose: comp, Model: 0, Final: 0, pctAdj: 0 };
  });
  const xMax = d3.max(data, d => Math.max(d.Model, d.Final)) || 1;
  const xLabel = cvmMetric === "trips" ? "Daily Trips" : "Daily VMT";

  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: 340,
    height: 130,
    marginLeft: 55,
    marginRight: 55,
    marginTop: 8,
    y: {domain: extOrder, label: null},
    x: {label: xLabel, domain: [0, xMax], grid: true, nice: true, tickFormat: "~s"},
    marks: [
      Plot.link(data, {x1: "Model", x2: "Final", y: "Purpose", stroke: themeLinkGrey, strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "Model", y: "Purpose", fill: themeNeutral, r: 7, title: d => `${d.Purpose}\nUnadjusted: ${fmtInt(d.Model)}`}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "Final", y: "Purpose", fill: themeModel, r: 7, title: d => `${d.Purpose}\nFinal: ${fmtInt(d.Final)}`}),
      Plot.text(data, {x: "Final", y: "Purpose", text: d => d3.format("+.1f")(d.pctAdj) + "%", dx: 10, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 600, fill: themeNeutral}),
    ],
  });
  return html`<div>
    <div style="font-weight:600; text-align:center; margin-bottom:2px;">${vehicleLabel.get(veh)}</div>
    ${chart}
  </div>`;
}

html`<div><div style="display:flex; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap; justify-content:center;">${["MD", "HV"].map(externalDumbbell)}</div>
<p style="text-align:center; color:${themeNeutral}; font-size:0.9em;">Light commercial vehicles (LT) have no external-station component -- see note above.</p></div>`
```

```{ojs}

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      ${["Vehicle Type", "Movement", "Before Station Adjustment", "Final (Calibrated)", "Adjustment Factor"].map(d =>
        html`<th style='text-align:left; padding:5px;'>${d}</th>`)}
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    ${["MD", "HV"].flatMap(veh => extOrder.map(comp => {

      if (!r) return html``;
      return html`<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid lightgrey;'>

        <td style='padding:5px; text-align:right;'>${fmtInt(r.unfactored)}</td>
```

## Methodology & Caveats

- **Trip generation** figures are exact: `tdm/2_ModelScripts/2_TripGen/2_TripGen_CV.s`
  multiplies each zone's raw rate-model production by a county x vehicle-type
  (x vocation, for MD/HV) calibration factor, in place -- so the "base model"
  value here is the same production divided back out by that factor, not an
  estimate.
- **VMT** figures use an approximation: the calibration factor is unfactored
  from the origin (production) zone of each trip only. A trip's destination
  zone -- and, for IX trips, its external end -- carries its own factor too,
  which isn't undone here. This tends to pull the VMT adjustment slightly
  toward zero relative to what a full two-sided treatment would show. Treat
  the VMT split as directionally right, not to the same precision as trip
  generation.
- Produced by `scripts/cv_purpose_factoring.py` (run manually per calibration
  run; see that script's module docstring for the full mechanism and
  `scripts/cv_effective_factors.py` for the underlying per-zone factor
  reconstruction).
